lesson: Week 1, Lesson 1: What AI actually is, and how we got here

beats.text: Most people met AI in November 2022, when ChatGPT launched. The story starts much earlier, and knowing it will change how you use these tools.
beats.say: Most people met AI in November twenty twenty-two, when Chat G P T launched. The story starts much earlier, and knowing it will change how you use these tools.

beats.text: In this lesson, you'll learn where AI came from, what a language model does when it answers you, and how to get better answers from it.
In 1950, the British mathematician Alan Turing asked a practical question: could a machine hold a conversation so well that you couldn't tell it from a person?
beats.say: In nineteen fifty, the British mathematician Alan Turing asked a practical question: could a machine hold a conversation so well that you couldn't tell it from a person?

beats.text: He didn't try to answer whether machines can think. Nobody can measure that. He chose a question you could test.
This course uses the same kind of test. What matters is whether the output is good enough to use.
The early excitement didn't last. In the 1970s, and again in the late 1980s, the technology fell short of what had been promised, and funding was cut.
beats.say: The early excitement didn't last. In the nineteen seventies, and again in the late nineteen eighties, the technology fell short of what had been promised, and funding was cut.

beats.text: These periods are known as the AI winters.
Today's AI is far more capable, but the lesson still applies. Judge a tool by what it actually does for you.
By the end of this bootcamp, you'll have built enough with these tools to judge them yourself.
In 2017, researchers at Google published a paper called "Attention Is All You Need". It introduced the transformer, the design behind today's language models.

beats.text: In November 2022, OpenAI released ChatGPT, a simple chat window anyone could use. Within two months, it had an estimated hundred million users.

chapters.label: What a model is actually doing

beats.text: So what does a language model do? It predicts the next word. It learned patterns from a huge amount of text, and it uses them to work out which words are most likely to come next.
That explains its common mistakes. It can invent a source, because a real-sounding title is a likely thing to write next.
A vague request gets a generic answer, because the most common answer is the safest prediction.
And the same question can get different answers, because the model chooses between likely words each time.
Most important of all: the model doesn't know what you're trying to do. It only knows what you tell it.
Here's an example. Amaka runs a cake business in Lagos and sells on Instagram and WhatsApp.
beats.say: Here's an example. Ah-mah-kah runs a cake business in Lagos and sells on Instagram and WhatsApp.

beats.text: She asks ChatGPT for an Instagram caption for her cake business, and gets: "Indulge in our delicious, freshly baked cakes! Perfect for every occasion. Order now!"
beats.say: She asks Chat G P T for an Instagram caption for her cake business, and gets: Indulge in our delicious, freshly baked cakes! Perfect for every occasion. Order now!

beats.text: It's generic, because the only thing the model knew was the word "cake".

Then she adds the details: her business name, same-day delivery in Lekki for orders before 2pm, this week's red velvet at ₦25,000, customers planning last-minute birthdays, and a short, warm tone with no hashtags.
beats.say: Then she adds the details: her business name, same-day delivery in Lekki for orders before two p.m., this week's red velvet at twenty-five thousand naira, customers planning last-minute birthdays, and a short, warm tone with no hashtags.

beats.text: This time the caption is specific to her business, because her instructions were.
One more check: when a model gives you sources, open every link. Some won't exist.
To recap: a language model predicts the next word, based on what you give it.
So the quality of the answer depends on the detail in your request.
Try it now with your own work. Ask once in one line, then again with five lines of detail, and compare the two.
